question.problem:
The function $f(x),$ defined as 

$$
f(x)=\frac{2x+k}{x-1},\,x\ne 1
$$

has an inverse function given by 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{x-8}{x-2},\,x\ne 2.
$$

What is the value of $k?$
question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=\frac{2x+k}{x-1}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=\frac{2y+k}{y-1}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{2y+k}{y-1} \\ x(y-1) & =2y+k \\ xy-x & =2y+k \\ xy-2y & =x+k \\ y(x-2) & =x+k \\ y & =\frac{x+k}{x-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{x+k}{x-2}.
$$

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that $k=-8.$
